label: Strait of Hormuz
description: Disruption to commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of seaborne crude. The mechanisms this scenario routes through are the crude price, crude freight rates, marine war-risk premiums and refining crack spreads.
method: Illustrative. Every number in this file was authored by hand to exercise the scenario architecture end to end. None of it is calibrated against history, derived from a model, or elicited from a forecaster, and none of it is a MONAD forecast. It is here so that the strip, the drawer and the bay modules have a shaped, self-consistent scenario to render while the modelling work that would replace it is done.
provenance: hand-authored fixture, docs/research/SCREENER_IA_DRAFT_PLAN.md scenario layer Phase B
partition: The deepest shortfall in daily commercial transits through the strait, measured against the trailing-year baseline and sustained for at least 7 consecutive days, at any point within the horizon. The four branches are half-open intervals on that one quantity — [0,5), [5,20), [20,50), [50,100] percent — so every value falls in exactly one, and their union is the whole range. Endpoints are stated as digits and not in words on purpose, twice over: 'no material shortfall' and 'a limited shortfall of under a fifth' both describe a 1% reading, so a tree built from overlapping English sums to 1 while double-counting; and the 5 and the 7 here are checked against the target's threshold_pct and min_days, which a spelled-out 'seven' would defeat. 'Material' for this scenario means a shortfall of at least 5% on this definition — and that is now enforced rather than promised.
